name: CyberGhost
tagline: A consumer VPN with one plan sold on 1-month, 6-month and 2-year terms.
bestFor: Streaming and everyday privacy on up to 7 devices
description: CyberGhost is a consumer VPN run from Bucharest, Romania, with servers in 100+ countries and WireGuard among its protocols. It sells a single plan on 1-month, 6-month and 2-year terms, and the longer terms renew yearly after an introductory first period.
pros: 45-day money-back guarantee on 6-month and longer terms
No-logs policy audited by Deloitte Audit Romania three times (2022, 2024, 2025)
Content Blocker and Identity Guard included in every plan
cons: Only 14-day refund window on the 1-month plan

plans.name: CyberGhost VPN
plans.notes: Single plan. No 1-year term is sold, so annual is null. 1 month: $12.99, renews at $12.99 a month. 6 months: $6.99/mo ($41.94 every 6 months, renews at $41.94 every 6 months). 2 years + 4 free months: $2.19/mo ($61.32 for the first 28 months), then renews at $61.32 a year. Prices are third-party reports: CyberGhost's site returned a bot-check page (HTTP 403) and could not be read. 7 simultaneous connections. Dedicated IP and Security Suite (Windows) are paid add-ons.

research.audit: Deloitte Audit Romania, no-logs assurance reports in 2022, 2024 and 2025 (ISAE 3000)
research.notes: Every cyberghostvpn.com page (buy, pricing, checkout) returned a Cloudflare bot-check (HTTP 403) to curl, WebFetch and the built-in browser, so no price was read on the vendor's own page; all prices are from Gizmodo's November 2026 table and the pricingsaas.com tracker of CyberGhost's pricing page. The tracker logged the 2-year offer changing on 9 Nov 2026 from 2 years + 2 months ($56.94) to 2 years + 4 months ($61.32) at the same $2.19/mo; a search snippet of an older official checkout page read 'valid for the first 26 months, then $56.94 yearly', which matches the pattern of the 2-year plan renewing yearly at its first-term upfront amount. CyberGhost's own support article (updated 8 Nov 2026) says longer offers 'renew annually at the standard rate' with the exact figure shown at checkout. Currency assumed USD from the $ sign in both third-party sources. Money-back is 45 days on 6-month and longer terms, 14 days on 1-month (not for app-store purchases). Split tunneling confirmed on Android (App Split Tunnel); Windows has a website-exceptions feature. Owned by Kape Technologies.

name: Mullvad
tagline: A Swedish VPN with one flat price, numbered accounts and no email needed to sign up.
bestFor: Privacy-focused users who want to pay anonymously
description: Mullvad is a VPN from Mullvad VPN AB in Gothenburg, Sweden, that uses account numbers instead of email sign-ups and accepts cash and cryptocurrency. It charges a flat 5 EUR a month whatever the length of time bought, with up to 5 devices per account.
pros: Same flat price for any term, so no renewal price jump
Accepts cash, Monero and Bitcoin as well as cards and PayPal
Regular published third-party audits of apps and VPN servers
cons: Priced only in EUR, no USD price

plans.name: Mullvad VPN
plans.notes: Flat 5 EUR per month including VAT for any length bought (1 month, 1 year or 1 decade). Mullvad publishes no USD price (its pricing page shows about $5.51 only as a conversion of 5 EUR), so USD fields are null. No introductory discount, so the price does not rise at renewal. Up to 5 devices.

research.notes: Prices null because Mullvad charges only in EUR; the pricing page shows $5.51 purely as a currency conversion of 5 EUR, not as a USD price. There is no 2-year option and no tiers. The 14-day money-back guarantee excludes cash payments. Kill switch: always on in the desktop app while connected, plus an optional lockdown mode. Split tunneling (exclude apps) on Windows, macOS 13+, Linux and Android, not iOS. Recent audits on Mullvad's blog also include X41 D-Sec (account and payment services, Jan 2026), Assured Security Consultants (GotaTun WireGuard implementation, Mar 2026) and Leviathan Security Group (Android app, Jun 2026); the most recent audit that explicitly covered logging on VPN servers is 2024 (Cure53) / 2022 (Assured AB). 'Founded 2009' is the service launch date (March 2009) on Mullvad's About page.

name: IPVanish
tagline: A US-based VPN with unlimited simultaneous connections and three tiers that add antivirus and cloud storage.
bestFor: Households that want to cover any number of devices
description: IPVanish is a VPN owned by Ziff Davis that does not limit simultaneous connections and runs 3,100+ servers. It sells Essential, Complete and Advanced tiers on monthly, yearly and 2-year terms, and the yearly and 2-year plans renew yearly at a higher price after the first term.
pros: Unlimited simultaneous connections on every tier
Renewal prices listed on the pricing page
No-logs policy audited by Leviathan (2022) and Schellman (2025, 2026)
cons: Yearly and 2-year plans renew at $99.99 a year or more
2-year plans switch to yearly billing after the first term

plans.name: Essential
plans.notes: VPN, Threat Protection, 24/7 live chat, 3GB eSIM data, unlimited devices. Monthly renews monthly at $14.99. 1-year: $46.68 for the first year, then renews at $99.99/year. 2-year: $2.19/mo, $52.56 for the first 2 years, then renews at $99.99/year (yearly cycle).

plans.name: Complete
plans.notes: Adds next-gen antivirus and phone support. Monthly renews at $15.99. 1-year: $57.48 for the first year, then $109.99/year. 2-year: $2.79/mo, $66.96 for the first 2 years, then $109.99/year.

plans.name: Advanced
plans.notes: Adds 1TB cloud storage, Secure Browser and 2GB bonus eSIM data (5GB total). Monthly renews at $17.99. 1-year: $64.68 for the first year, then $129.99/year. 2-year: $3.29/mo, $78.96 for the first 2 years, then $129.99/year.

name: Windscribe
tagline: A Canadian VPN with a permanent free plan, a Pro plan and a pay-per-location Build A Plan option.
bestFor: Free VPN use and paying only for the locations you need
description: Windscribe is a VPN from Toronto, Canada, that offers a free plan with 10GB a month, a Pro plan with all locations, and a Build A Plan option priced per location. Every plan, including the free one, allows unlimited simultaneous connections.
pros: Permanent free plan with 10GB/month on 10 countries
Unlimited simultaneous connections, including on the free plan
Build A Plan from $3/month for selected locations
cons: Refunds only within 7 days and under 10GB used
Build A Plan data is capped at 10GB per chosen location
freePlanDetails: 10GB/month with a confirmed email (2GB without), servers in 10 countries, unlimited devices; extra data for posting about Windscribe on X (5GB/month) or referrals (1GB each).

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: All locations, unlimited data, R.O.B.E.R.T blocker, config generator (OpenVPN, IKEv2, WireGuard). Monthly $9.00 billed every month; yearly $69 billed every 12 months ($5.75/mo). Renews automatically; the pricing page shows no separate renewal price. Black Friday promo until 30 Nov 2026: Pro yearly $29 ($2.42/mo), 'Renews at $29 yearly. Forever.'

plans.name: Build A Plan
plans.notes: $1.00 per location per month with a $3 minimum (3 locations); each location adds 10GB to the monthly data allowance; up to 7 locations. Billed monthly, renews automatically. An 'Unlimited Data + R.O.B.E.R.T' add-on is offered; its price was not shown in the page text.

Windscribe does not advertise introductory pricing on the standard page, but it does not state a renewal figure either, so renewalUpfront is null. The homepage Black Friday banner links to a promo-code page with Pro yearly at $29 and the text 'Renews at $29 yearly. Forever.' (ends 30 Nov 2026); on that promo page the monthly box also displayed $29.00, which looks like a page glitch and was not used. Refunds: within 7 days of the first purchase and under 10GB used; renewals are not refundable. auditedNoLogs is null: Windscribe's audit page lists only infrastructure and app audits, not a no-logs audit; secondary sources say the 2024 Packetlabs test found no attempt to bypass the no-logs policy, and a 2025 Greek court case is cited by Windscribe as testing its policy, but neither is a no-logs audit. The firewall acts as the kill switch. Split tunneling on Windows, macOS, Linux and Android.

research.audit: KPMG no-log assessments (2020, and a second 'always-on' evaluation in 2021); PureVPN reports a fourth assessment in 2023 by an audit firm not named in the text read
research.notes: Plan prices are from the /order checkout page (Black Friday deal live today), which is internally consistent (upfront / months = per-month). The /pricing page shows different and inconsistent figures (2-year $2.15/$2.73/$3.55 per month but 'billed $57.95/$89.95/$109.95'; 1-year $2.55/$4.55/$5.55 per month but 'billed $47.95/$69.95/$84.95', which match renewal amounts) and lists Plus monthly at $15.95 rather than $17.95, so those were not used. Renewal prices come from the official Subscription Renewal Prices page (USD, before tax): Standard 1-month $12.95, 1-year $57.95, 2-year and 5-year $47.95/year; Plus 1-month $15.95, 1-year $69.95, 2-year and 5-year $69.95/year; Max 1-month $19.95, 1-year $89.95, 2-year and 5-year $84.95/year; these match the checkout 'then auto-renews at' text. Fetch note: this network's DNS returned a non-working address for www.purevpn.com, so the three PureVPN pages were fetched by pointing at the Cloudflare address that public DNS (1.1.1.1) gives for the site; a later attempt to fetch more PureVPN pages that way was blocked by the session's permission check, so audit and feature details come from PureVPN's support site and search results. Kill switch, split tunneling (Windows, Android) and WireGuard are confirmed on PureVPN's support site. A 3GB eSIM data bonus is listed on all tiers.
